log.why: Ticket 1 expires sooner; E9 splits the posterior almost evenly (0.506 vs 0.494) for maximum information gain.
Ticket 2 has no plates growing, and testing 10 uM splits the posterior mass most evenly (0.437 vs 0.563).
Ticket 1 expires sooner, and testing leading candidate ftsZ (posterior 0.332) can raise it to ~0.85 if positive or leave gyrA and ompF.
Testing 30 µM on Ticket 2 splits the posterior nearly evenly (0.467 vs 0.533) between 30 µM or less and higher thresholds.
Ticket 1 is most urgent (57s left); knocking out gyrA directly tests the 46.1% top candidate.
Ticket 2 has 59s left with 100 uM vs 300 uM unresolved; E6 cleanly separates them while Ticket 1 incubates.
Ticket 3 has 54 s left and flat posteriors; E9 splits probability nearly in half (0.470) to start incubation immediately.
E9 tests {recA, trpE, katG} (posterior mass 0.562), maximizing information gain on Ticket 4 while an incubator is free before publishing Ticket 1.
Posterior for 100 uM is 0.815, and with 14 s left there is insufficient time to run and read another experiment.
Ticket 3 has 22 s left with hisG and gyrA close; E2 separates them in one plate before publishing.
Testing recA on Ticket 4 pipelines well while Ticket 3's E2 incubates, and strongly confirms or rules out recA.
E3 splits Ticket 5 posterior nearly evenly (0.540 vs 0.460) and lets incubation overlap with publishing Ticket 4 next.
Publish Ticket 4 claiming recA at 0.941 posterior before its 15 s deadline expires.
With 26 s left, testing 10 uM cleanly splits Ticket 5's top hypotheses (0.563 vs 0.437) so it can publish quickly.
Split Ticket 6 near 50/50 with E7 while E4 incubates on Ticket 5, leaving time to publish both before round end.
